name: GroupGenerator_init
reason: The initial state (i = 0, previous = 0) is passed by insertThousandsGrouping and pinned by GroupingPlacement and insert_doc: a nonzero previous would group the C locale's empty grouping, which insert_doc refuses.

name: GroupGenerator_next
reason: Every theorem uses only the groupings [g], [CHAR_MAX] and [] (get_locale_info is fixed to the C locale), so a generator that never advances i and always returns grouping[0] passes; the walk through a multi-entry locale grouping such as "\3\2", which 'n' reaches under setlocale, is never constrained.

name: InsertThousandsGrouping_fill
reason: groupPiece and groupPieceFwd mirror the backward and forward copies, and GroupingPlacement and GroupingFraction pin where the zeros, digits and separators land against groupFR and groupFL; the counting-mode maxchar update is not observable.

name: _PyUnicode_InsertThousandsGrouping
reason: groupLoop mirrors the loop, the break and the post-loop branch; GroupingPlacement pins separator placement, the fewest leading zeros that reach min_width and count = length for every repeated size, and insert_doc covers the no-grouping (post-loop) branch.

name: unknown_presentation_type
reason: StrFormatSpecDoc and the entry theorems compare against unknownTypeMessage, the message written out independently (both the %c and the \x%x branch are reachable through the TypeChar tail, and tp_name is cut to 200 bytes as %.200s does).

name: invalid_thousands_separator_type
reason: ParseDoc compares against sepTypeMessage, written out from :272-279, for every separator and type character the grammar allows, so both branches (types >= 128 and below 33 reach the hex one) are pinned.

name: invalid_comma_and_underscore
reason: ParseDoc covers ',_' and '_,' after the width and after the precision (groupingValue), including the precision-side call sites :511 and :523.

name: get_integer
reason: ParseDoc reads width and precision as runs of decimal digits of any script (Py_UNICODE_TODECIMAL) and any length, with 'Too many decimal digits in format string' above PY_SSIZE_T_MAX, in the order the parser meets them.

name: is_alignment_token
reason: ParseDoc distinguishes alignment from fill and type for all four tokens and for non-tokens (a TypeChar tail must not be read as an alignment), so a constant function fails.

name: is_sign_element
reason: ParseDoc requires the sign field (+, -, space) to be read as the sign and every other character not to be, so neither constant function passes.

name: parse_internal_render_format_spec
reason: ParseDoc: parseFormatSpec equals the documented reading docParse for every spec written from the grammar's fields, including sign, z, #, the 0 option, separators, doubled separators, overflow, missing precision, invalid specifier and the per-type separator checks; the refuted frac-separator entry has its bug record.

name: calc_padding
reason: StrInternalDoc pins it against docFormat for every parsed spec, width -1 included (SpecInv allows it), for <, > and ^; '=' never reaches it from str or complex.

name: fill_padding
reason: StrInternalDoc pins the left and right fill around the content against docFormat for every parsed spec.

name: parse_number
reason: FloatFormatDoc pins the digits/point/fraction/remainder split against docFloatLayout for every spec, including fraction separators, so a parse that folds the fraction into the remainder or stops the digits early fails.

name: calc_number_widths
reason: calc_doc (int, prefix) and fullCore (float, fraction and decimal) pin the sign switch, the alignment switch and n_min_width against docNumber (fewest zeros reaching the width, padding per alignment) inside IntFormatDoc and FloatFormatDoc for every parsed spec.

name: fill_number
reason: The field order, toupper on prefix and digits for X, and the decimal, grouped fraction and remainder are pinned against docNumber by IntFormatDoc and FloatFormatDoc; the non-ascii SystemError is unreachable as the model argues.

name: get_locale_info
reason: The LT_CURRENT_LOCALE branch is replaced by the C locale's constants instead of taking localeconv() as an input, so the 'n' type under any other locale (its decimal point, thousands_sep and grouping) and the _Py_GetLocaleconvNumeric failure path are not modelled.

name: free_locale_info
reason: no-behaviour applies: it only drops references to three str objects and frees the grouping copy, with no Python-visible effect.

name: format_string_internal
reason: StrInternalDoc: for every spec the parser returns, the four refusals in source order and otherwise the documented truncation and padding (docStr), fast path included.

name: format_long_internal
reason: IntFormatDoc: for every int, every parsed integer-type spec and either PyLong_CheckExact answer, the refusals, the c branch with its C long and range(0x110000) errors, all bases with #, sign, separators and zero padding, and the fast path equal the independent docInt.

name: format_float_internal
reason: FloatBufDoc pins the type, precision and flags handed to PyOS_double_to_string against docFloatBuf, and FloatFormatDoc pins 'precision too big' and the layout against docFloatLayout for every parsed spec, fast path included.

name: format_complex_internal
reason: ComplexPartsCompose needs a presentation type and ComplexOmittedTypeIsRepr needs no precision, no sign option and no width, so with the type omitted the 'r'-to-'g' switch under a precision, the sign kept for the imaginary part when the real part is skipped (format(2j, ' ')) and padding around the parentheses are only constrained by width-is-minimum.

name: format_obj
reason: Modelled as PyObject_Str's outcome, a fallible input, passed through with its exception; the entry theorems require it for the empty spec of every subclass.

name: _PyUnicode_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: StrFormatSpecDoc: empty spec gives the string (exact) or str(obj) with its exception (subclass), otherwise docParse, the s type as docStr, and Unknown format code with tp_name for every other type.

name: _PyLong_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: LongEntryDoc: empty spec gives docIntStr (exact, 4300-digit limit) or str(obj); integer types are docInt; float types run PyNumber_Float's outcome (fallible input) into docFloat; other types raise with tp_name.

name: _PyFloat_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: FloatEntryDoc pins the dispatch (empty spec is str(obj), the nine accepted types including a literal NUL, unknown type with tp_name); the NUL refutation has its bug record.

name: _PyComplex_FormatAdvancedWriter
reason: ComplexEntryDoc pins the dispatch (empty spec is str(obj), the accepted types without %, unknown type with tp_name); FloatComplexErrors and the NUL refutation cover its refusals.
